walkthroughs.body_html:
Biodiversity & Conservation — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Biodiversity & Conservation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Biodiversity & Conservation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Endemic
Endangered
Environmental
Extinct in nature

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils often nutrient-poor despite abundant vegetation?
options: Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
Rainforests have rich soils because they are productive.
Services that ecosystems perform for themselves.
Rapid decomposition and uptake mean nutrients cycle quickly through living biomass, not soil.

mcqs.q: What process moves carbon from the atmosphere into plants?
options: Services that ecosystems perform for themselves.
Respiration.
Photosynthesis.
Decomposition.
Government services that protect nature.
Benefits people obtain from ecosystems (pollination, water purification, climate regulation, food).
Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
Services that ecosystems perform for themselves.
